# 5 minute quickstart tutorial

Follow this example to get started with DeepInverse in under 5 minutes.

**Contents**

1. [Install](#install)
2. [Physics](#physics)
3. [Models](#models)
4. [Datasets](#datasets)
5. [What’s next](#what-s-next)

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 18-56 -->

## 1. Install

First, install and import the latest stable release of `deepinv`:

### pip

```bash
pip install deepinv
```

### uv

```bash
uv pip install deepinv
```

### pixi

```bash
pixi add --pypi deepinv
```

### conda

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge deepinv
```

We then get the device (CPU in the case of this example).

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 56-62 -->
```Python
import deepinv as dinv
import torch

device = dinv.utils.get_device()
```

```none

```

## 2. Physics

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 69-71 -->

In DeepInverse, `x` are images:

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 71-74 -->
```Python
x = dinv.utils.load_example("butterfly.png", device=device)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 75-76 -->

Images are tensors of shape `B, C, ...` where `B` is batch size, `C` are channels and `...` are spatial dimensions:

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 76-79 -->
```Python
print(x.shape)
```

```none
torch.Size([1, 3, 256, 256])
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 80-83 -->

[Imaging forward operators](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/physics/intro.html.md#physics-intro) are called `physics` and simulate
measurements `y` from `x`.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 83-89 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.Inpainting(x.shape[1:], mask=0.3, device=device)

y = physics(x)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 90-96 -->

DeepInverse implements
[many different types of physics](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/physics/physics.html.md#physics) across various imaging modalities.
Physics also possess noise models such as Gaussian or Poisson noise.

#### HINT
Do you get a matplotlib LaTeX error when plotting? Disable LaTeX using `dinv.utils.disable_tex()`

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 96-104 -->
```Python
physics.noise_model = dinv.physics.GaussianNoise(sigma=0.1)

y = physics(x)

dinv.utils.plot({"GT": x, "Noisy Inpainting \nMeasurement": y})
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 105-107 -->

Many physics also take
[physics parameters](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/physics/intro.html.md#parameter-dependent-operators) such as `mask`, `filter`, `sigma` etc.:

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 107-116 -->
```Python
# Blur with Gaussian filter parameter
filter = dinv.physics.functional.gaussian_blur(sigma=(5, 5))

physics = dinv.physics.BlurFFT(x.shape[1:], filter=filter, device=device)

# Simulate measurements
y = physics(x)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 117-119 -->

You can easily use your own params by passing these into the `physics`,
or you can use a `generator` to [generate random params](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/physics/intro.html.md#physics-generators):

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 119-141 -->
```Python
# Blur kernel random generator
physics_generator = dinv.physics.generator.MotionBlurGenerator(
    psf_size=(31, 31), num_channels=3, device=device
)

# Generate a dict of random params {"filter": ...}
params = physics_generator.step()

# Update physics during forward call
y2 = physics(x, **params)

dinv.utils.plot(
    {
        "GT": x,
        "Blurred...": y,
        "... with Gaussian kernel": filter,
        "Blurred ...": y2,
        "...with motion kernel": params["filter"],
    }
)
```


<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 142-145 -->

Physics are powerful objects and [have many methods](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/physics/intro.html.md#physics-intro), for example a
pseudo-inverse:

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 145-151 -->
```Python
# You can also update params like so
physics.update(filter=filter.to(device))

x_pinv = physics.A_dagger(y)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 152-154 -->

As it is well-known in the field of inverse problems, the pseudo-inverse can give good results
if the problem is noiseless, but it completely fails in the presence of noise - this is why we need reconstructors!

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 154-166 -->
```Python
physics.noise_model = dinv.physics.GaussianNoise(sigma=0.1)

y = physics(x)

x_pinv_noise = physics.A_dagger(y)

dinv.utils.plot(
    {"Pseudoinv \nw/o noise": x_pinv, "Pseudoinv \nwith noise": x_pinv_noise}
)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 167-171 -->

#### TIP
Want to use DeepInverse with your own physics operator? Check out [Bring your own physics](https://deepinv.org/auto_examples/basics/demo_custom_physics.html.md#sphx-glr-auto-examples-basics-demo-custom-physics-py) for a tutorial!

## 3. Models

In DeepInverse, a `model` is a reconstruction algorithm that
**reconstructs** images from `y` and knowledge of `physics`.

#### TIP
Many models, such as [`Reconstruct Anything Model`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.models.RAM.html.md#deepinv.models.RAM), are [pretrained reconstructors](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/reconstruction/pretrained-models.html.md#pretrained-models) and can
be used out of the box. See [Use a pretrained model](https://deepinv.org/auto_examples/basics/demo_pretrained_model.html.md#sphx-glr-auto-examples-basics-demo-pretrained-model-py) for a full example.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 184-189 -->
```Python
model = dinv.models.RAM(pretrained=True, device=device)

x_hat = model(y, physics)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 190-193 -->

Plot the image `x`, the measurement `y` and the reconstructed image
`x_hat` and compute [metrics](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/training/metric.html.md#metric):

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 193-208 -->
```Python
metric = dinv.metric.PSNR()

psnr_y = metric(y, x).item()
psnr_x_hat = metric(x_hat, x).item()

dinv.utils.plot(
    {
        "Ground Truth": x,
        "Measurement": y,
        "Reconstruction": x_hat,
    },
    subtitles=["PSNR:", f"{psnr_y:.2f} dB", f"{psnr_x_hat:.2f} dB"],
)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 209-213 -->

Some models are only [denoisers](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/reconstruction/denoisers.html.md#denoisers) that **denoise**
images from `y` and `sigma`, which can be used to build many
[model-based reconstruction algorithms](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/reconstruction/iterative.html.md#iterative).

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 213-237 -->
```Python
denoiser = dinv.models.DRUNet(device=device)

x_denoised = denoiser(y, sigma=0.1)

model = dinv.optim.DPIR(sigma=0.1, denoiser=denoiser, device=device)

x_hat = model(y, physics)

dinv.utils.plot(
    {
        "Ground Truth": x,
        "Measurement": y,
        "Denoised": x_denoised,
        "Reconstruction": x_hat,
    },
    subtitles=[
        "PSNR:",
        f"{dinv.metric.PSNR()(y, x).item():.2f} dB",
        f"{dinv.metric.PSNR()(x_denoised, x).item():.2f} dB",
        f"{dinv.metric.PSNR()(x_hat, x).item():.2f} dB",
    ],
)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 238-243 -->

DeepInverse covers
[many frameworks of reconstruction algorithms](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/reconstruction/introduction.html.md#reconstructors)
including [deep model architectures](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/reconstruction/deep-reconstructors.html.md#deep-reconstructors), [iterative algorithms](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/reconstruction/iterative.html.md#iterative), [sampling algorithms](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/reconstruction/sampling.html.md#sampling)
(e.g. diffusion models), and [unfolded models](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/reconstruction/unfolded.html.md#unfolded).

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 243-247 -->
```Python
# Reconstruct Anything Model foundation model
model = dinv.models.RAM(pretrained=True, device=device)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 248-252 -->

#### TIP
Want to use DeepInverse with your own network? Just inherit from the reconstructor base class [`deepinv.models.Reconstructor`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.models.Reconstructor.html.md#deepinv.models.Reconstructor)!

## 4. Datasets

You can use DeepInverse with [dataset](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/training/datasets.html.md#datasets), for testing or training. First,
define a ground-truth dataset. We implement wrappers for
[many popular imaging datasets](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/training/datasets.html.md#datasets) across domains including natural images,
medical imaging, satellite imaging, etc.

#### TIP
It’s easy to use your own dataset with DeepInverse. See [Bring your own dataset](https://deepinv.org/auto_examples/basics/demo_custom_dataset.html.md#sphx-glr-auto-examples-basics-demo-custom-dataset-py) for a tutorial.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 266-272 -->
```Python
dataset = dinv.datasets.SimpleFastMRISliceDataset(
    "data", anatomy="brain", download=True
)
```

```none
100%|██████████| 801k/801k [00:00<00:00, 7.14MB/s]
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 273-277 -->

[Datasets](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/training/datasets.html.md#datasets) return either `x`, tuples `x, y` or `x, y, params` of images,
measurements, and optional physics parameters. Given a ground-truth
dataset, you can simulate a dataset with random physics:

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 277-297 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.MRI(device=device)

physics_generator = dinv.physics.generator.RandomMaskGenerator(
    (320, 320), device=device
)

path = dinv.datasets.generate_dataset(
    dataset,
    physics,
    save_dir="data",
    physics_generator=physics_generator,
    device=device,
)

dataset = dinv.datasets.HDF5Dataset(
    path, load_physics_generator_params=True, use_dict_output=True
)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 300-312 -->
```Python
import torch

dinv.test(
    model,
    torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset),
    physics,
    plot_images=True,
    device=device,
)
```
